unit.can_do_en: get a library card and borrow a book.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Anteeks, onks teil helppoja suomenkielisiä kirjoja?
lines.text_kirja: Anteeksi, onko teillä helppoja suomenkielisiä kirjoja?
lines.gloss_en: Excuse me, do you have easy books in Finnish?

judge.reason: Same question; only register differences (anteeks/anteeksi, onks/onko, teil/teillä).

lines.speaker: Outi
lines.gloss_en: Yes. The easy-read books are on that shelf.

judge.reason: Same content: yes, easy-reading books are over there on the shelf; on/ovat and hyllys/hyllyssä are register differences.

lines.speaker: Outi
lines.text_puhe: Se on kirja, jossa on helppoo suomee.
lines.text_kirja: Se on kirja, jossa on helppoa suomea.
lines.gloss_en: It's a book in easy Finnish.

judge.reason: Same meaning; helppoo suomee is spoken for helppoa suomea.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Täydellistä! Kauanks mä saan pitää sen?
lines.text_kirja: Täydellistä! Kauanko minä saan pitää sen?
lines.gloss_en: Perfect! How long can I keep it?

judge.reason: Same question about how long I may keep it; kauanks/mä vs kauanko/minä.

lines.speaker: Outi
lines.text_puhe: Neljä viikkoo. Sä voit uusii lainan netissä.
lines.text_kirja: Neljä viikkoa. Sinä voit uusia lainan verkossa.
lines.gloss_en: Four weeks. You can renew the loan online.

judge.reason: Same: four weeks, you can renew the loan online; netissä and verkossa both mean online.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Good. Where do I check it out?

judge.reason: Same question: where do I borrow it from; mist/mä vs mistä/minä.

lines.speaker: Outi
lines.text_puhe: Tost automaatist. Laita vaan kortti siihen.
lines.text_kirja: Tuosta automaatista. Laita vain kortti siihen.
lines.gloss_en: From that machine. Just put your card in.

judge.reason: Same: from that machine over there, just put the card in; spoken forms only.

forms.why_en: Means 'excuse me', a polite way to get someone's attention before asking.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Means 'is...?'. The question ending -ko turns 'on' (is) into a question.
Adessive plural of 'te' (you): 'teillä' with 'onko' means 'do you (all) have'.
Describing an open number of things takes -ja: helppo becomes helppoja.
Describing an open number of things takes -iä: suomenkielinen becomes suomenkielisiä.
The partitive plural is used for some books: kirja becomes kirjoja.
Means 'is': present tense, 3rd person singular, going with 'Helsinki'.
Adds -t for more than one: selkokirja becomes selkokirjat.
Books write ovat for 'they are'. Speech uses on for one thing or many.
Tuo, that, with -lla: tuolla, over there.
Adds -ssä for 'in' or 'on': hylly becomes hyllyssä. Speech drops the last vowel: hyllys.
'What.' A question word in nominative singular, asking what the price is.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
'It.' Nominative singular, referring back to the price.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
joka means which. Adding -ssa gives jossa, 'in which'.
Saying what something is like takes -a: helppo becomes helppoa. Speech turns -oa into -oo.
The partitive adds -a after puhua, to speak: suomea. Speech turns -ea into -ee.
The partitive singular is used in exclamations: täydellinen becomes täydellistä.
Kauan, long, with -ko to ask. Speech says -ks: kauanks.
Means 'I'. Spoken Finnish often says 'mä'.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to get, to be allowed to
forms.why_en: Saada drops -da and takes -n for 'I': saan.

forms.meaning_en: to have to, to like, to hold

forms.why_en: This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Se with -n when the whole thing is the object: kirjoittaa sen.
'Four.' The number stays in nominative singular; the counted word after it changes form.
After a number above one, the noun takes the partitive singular: viikko becomes viikkoa. Speech says viikkoo.
Means 'you' (one person). Spoken: 'sä'.
Voida drops -da and takes -t for 'you': voit.
A whole thing acted on takes -n: laina becomes lainan.
Books write verkossa, 'in the network'. Speech says netissä, from netti, 'the net'.
Means 'good!' or 'great!', showing you are happy.
Means 'from where?'; the elative ending -stä means 'from'. Spoken: 'mist'.
Adds -sta for 'from': tuo becomes tuosta. Speech says tost.
Adds -sta for 'from': automaatti becomes automaatista, tt turning into t. Speech says automaatist.
This is how you tell someone to put: laita. It comes from laittaa, with one t.
Speech says vaan. Books write vain.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The illative singular of se 'it': siihen, 'into it, for it'. People say it the same way.
